chunks: 5315 - Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him:
That ʿAlī, peace be upon him, ruled concerning a man who was struck until his urine became continuous that the full diyyah applies.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ الْكَامِلَةِ: the full prescribed blood money for a serious bodily injury
key_terms.سَلِسَ بَوْلُهُ: continuous urinary incontinence resulting from injury
key_terms.قَضَى: issued a legal judgment or ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone is injured until he suffers continuous urinary incontinence?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding severe bodily injury. It establishes that when a beating causes continuous urinary incontinence, the injured person is entitled to the full blood money (diyyah), indicating the gravity of such permanent bodily harm in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5315 - It was narrated by Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that:
"Indeed, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ruled concerning a man who was struck until he suffered from continuous urination (incontinence) that he is entitled to the full blood money (diyyah)."
